title: Broken: a ForEach loads one wrong table instead of three
objective_text: Find why a ForEach runs once over a whole string, convert a text parameter into the list it stands for, and keep the pipeline driven by the parameter.
scenario: The schedule passes the tables to load as text, 'customers, orders,stores', typed by hand with uneven spaces. The run succeeds, but it copied one table called 'customers, orders,stores' and nothing else. Make the pipeline load the three tables the text names.
engine_label: Local pipeline runner on this PC (control flow only)
verifies: Your repaired pipeline JSON ran on the local runner on this PC with the schedule's text parameter and looped over the three table names, trimmed.
does_not_verify: Copying data: the Copy activity here is a stand-in with a fixed result, so no data moves and no connection is tested.
How a Fabric schedule or trigger passes parameter types; check your trigger's parameter settings in the workspace.

fault.summary: The tables parameter is text, and createArray() wraps the whole text as one item instead of splitting it.

planted.what: uneven spaces after commas, so a plain split leaves ' orders'

fault.symptom: The run succeeds but returns loaded = 'bronze.customers, orders,stores'.

validation.pass: The pipeline loads the three tables the text names.
validation.fail: Look at what loaded returned: one item, or names with spaces?

hints: The run succeeded, so read its return value: how many tables did the loop see?
split(text, ',') turns the text into a list, but ' orders' keeps its leading space.
Remove the spaces first: split(replace(pipeline().parameters.tables, ' ', ''), ','). Don't hard-code the names: tomorrow's list will differ.
explanation: A pipeline parameter has a type. When a schedule or caller passes text where a list is meant, a loop can run once over the whole text and still succeed, the most dangerous kind of failure. Convert at the boundary: split the text into an array and clean each part (here by removing spaces; trim() inside the loop also works). Better still, declare the parameter as an Array and pass a JSON list from the caller. A run that succeeds with the wrong result is found by checking outputs, not just status.
reset: Reset puts the broken pipeline.json back.
review_notes: Before live: confirm both remediation links load.
A pipeline that hard-codes these three names would pass. A second parameter set needs pipeline_lab support for several runs.
